summary: Millrose is diversifying away from Lennar on or slightly ahead of its 2026 plan (more than 40% non-Lennar by year-end): non-Lennar invested capital went from about $1.1B in mid-2025 to $3.4B at 2026-09-30 (36% of $9.2B), and about 42% pro forma for the October 2026 Dream Finders/Beazer financing, across 21 non-Lennar counterparties. Non-Lennar paper earns about 10.6-10.8% (floating over SOFR, floors around 10%) against a fixed 8.5% from Lennar, and management has said openly it accepts yield drifting toward 11% or lower in exchange for pooling and stronger builders. Its edge with builders is no longer just lot options: it now finances whole acquisitions (Rausch Coleman, Landsea, Beazer), writes preferred equity (a $500M, 12% Dream Finders instrument), funds build-to-rent (Taylor Morrison's Yardly) and multifamily land (JPI), with Kennedy Lewis signing the commitment and allocating between its funds and Millrose. Only five non-Lennar names are public (New Home/Risewell, Taylor Morrison, Dream Finders, Beazer, JPI); a top-10 public builder added in Q1 2026 and three additions in Q3 2026 are unnamed. The whole executive team is Kennedy Lewis staff (Richman, Nitkin, Rosenblum, Presa, Pasha) unchanged since the February 2025 spin-off, with a five-person fully independent board and no Lennar or Kennedy Lewis directors; Nitkin is the deal-facing voice on pricing and underwriting. Pressure points a rival can use: leverage is above target (36% vs 33%), the stock trades below book so equity is closed, Taylor Morrison is now owned by Berkshire Hathaway, and a short-seller report on Millrose buying Lennar's finished homes has put the Lennar relationship under scrutiny.

facts.fact: At 2026-09-30 Millrose reported 22 distinct counterparties (Lennar plus 21 others); no counterparty has walked from an option since inception. Invested capital was $9,245M: $5,874M under the Lennar Master Program Agreement (about 64%, calculated) and $3,371M under Other Agreements (about 36%, calculated; includes $175M of preferred-instrument funding). Other Agreements grew $521M in the quarter while Lennar fell from $5,949M.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Weighted average yield at 2026-09-30: 8.5% on the Lennar Master Program Agreement, 10.8% on Other Agreements, 9.3% blended. Weighted average remaining life 3.8 years (Lennar) vs 2.4 years (other); implied quarterly income run rate $128M Lennar vs $93M other.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Q3 2026 flows: land acquisition and development funding $1,260M ($546M Lennar, $714M other counterparties); homesite takedown proceeds $814M ($621M Lennar, $193M other). Non-Lennar deployment exceeded Lennar deployment in the quarter. Pro forma for the Dream Finders/Beazer closing on 2026-10-20, about 42% of the asset base sits outside the Lennar agreement.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Millrose has no employees of its own in the executive suite: all five executive officers (CEO/President Richman, COO Nitkin, CFO/Treasurer Rosenblum, GC/Secretary Presa, CTO Pasha) are employees of the manager, Kennedy Lewis Land and Residential Advisors LLC, and took their titles on 2025-02-07 (spin-off date). No Chief Investment Officer, head of capital markets or named investor-relations officer is published; none of the five sits on the board.
facts.source_title: Millrose 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-02)

facts.fact: The board has five directors, all seated 2025-02-07 and all deemed independent under NYSE rules: Carlos Migoya (Chair), Patrick Bartels, Matthew Gorson, Kathleen Lynch and M. Alison Mincey. The proxy describes none as affiliated with Lennar or Kennedy Lewis. All five were re-nominated for the 2026-05-18 annual meeting.
facts.source_title: Millrose 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-02)

facts.fact: The company team page (opened 2026-11-19) still lists the same five executives and five directors as the April 2026 proxy, and the filing list shows no Item 5.02 8-K (officer/director change) since the spin-off 8-K of 2025-02-07, so the roster is unchanged as of November 2026.
facts.source_title: Millrose Properties website, Our Team

facts.fact: Lennar no longer holds a meaningful stake: it kept about 20% of Class A stock at the spin-off, then disposed of it through an exchange offer that closed 2025-11-28, leaving a 'de minimis' holding. Lennar's influence now runs through contracts (Master Program Agreement, Founder's Rights Agreement), not ownership or board seats.
facts.source_title: Millrose 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-02)

facts.fact: Management fee expensed to Kennedy Lewis for 2025 was about $87.8M; the manager pays non-employee director fees up to $1.25M a year (rising 3% annually). 2025 related-party flows with Lennar: $484.8M of option fee revenue, $2,862M of land acquisition and development funding, $3,167M of net takedown proceeds. The Rausch Coleman land purchase (2025-02-10) cost about $859M cash for roughly 25,000 homesites.
facts.source_title: Millrose 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, filed 2026-04-02)

facts.fact: Published offices: headquarters 600 Brickell Avenue, Suite 1400, Miami, FL 33131; 225 Liberty Street, Suite 4210, New York, NY 10281; and 501 Office Center Drive, 3rd Floor, Fort Washington, PA 19034. No phone number and no named investor-relations contact are published; the contact page shows only obfuscated email links, and press releases route media to FGS Global (MillroseProperties@fgsglobal.com).
facts.source_title: Millrose Properties website, Contact

facts.fact: Counterparty count by quarter, as stated by management: 11 at 2025-06-30 (6 in the top 25 of the Zonda Builder 100), 12 at 2025-09-30, 15 at 2025-12-31 (9 of the top 25 US builders), 17 at 2026-03-31, 19 at 2026-06-30, 22 at 2026-09-30 (three added in Q3 2026). Counts include Lennar. Sources: Q2 2025, Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 call transcripts, Q1 2026 press release, Q2 and Q3 2026 decks; this row cites the latest.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Q1 2026: Millrose reached 17 homebuilders (16 outside Lennar) and said one of the two added in the quarter is a top-10 national homebuilder (the call specified publicly traded). It has never named that builder. Management said new relationships start small and grow, and that this one did not cause the quarter's yield dip.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-05-06)

facts.fact: Only five non-Lennar counterparties are publicly identifiable: New Home Co (now Risewell Homes), Taylor Morrison (for-sale program and Yardly build-to-rent), Dream Finders Homes, Beazer Homes (now part of Dream Finders) and JPI (multifamily). On the Q2 2025 call the CEO said he names only clients who have disclosed the relationship themselves. The other roughly 16 are undisclosed.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2025 earnings call transcript (Investing.com) (count of named builders compiled by this agent from the sources in builder_relationships)

facts.fact: Non-Lennar ('Other Agreements') weighted average yield by quarter: 11.4% (2025-06-30), 11.3% (2025-09-30), about 11% on recent investments (Q4 2025 call), 10.7% (2026-03-31), 10.6% (2026-06-30), 10.8% (2026-09-30). The Lennar Master Program rate held at 8.5% throughout 2026. The spread of non-Lennar over Lennar is therefore about 210 to 230 bps in 2026 (calculated: 10.6-10.8% minus 8.5%).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27); earlier quarters from the Q2/Q3/Q4 2025 call transcripts, Q1 2026 press release and Q2 2026 deck

facts.fact: COO Robert Nitkin on the Q3 2026 call: non-Lennar option agreements are generally floating rate over SOFR with contractual floors; the Q3 rise from 10.6% to 10.8% came from higher SOFR and new deals; he expects about 11% on Other Agreements in Q4 2026 once the Dream Finders deals are in for a full period.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Floors: on the Q4 2025 call Nitkin said floors on non-Lennar agreements sit on average 50 to 200 bps below the then-current rate; on the Q1 2026 call he put the average floor at about 10%. The Q1 2026 drop of about 30 bps in the non-Lennar yield was attributed entirely to lower SOFR; management said option spreads over the base rate were unchanged and rates on new deals were holding steady.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool, 2026-05-06)

facts.fact: On the Q2 2025 call CEO Richman said he expected the non-Lennar yield to drift down toward about 11% as the book grew, a deliberate trade for credit enhancements; Nitkin added that recent deals priced lower because of builder selection and pooling, and that yields would be higher without those protections. The Lennar rate is fixed, subject to resets on forward deals (Q4 2025 call).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2025 earnings call transcript (Investing.com)

facts.fact: Dream Finders preferred: 12% cumulative dividend on a $500M balance, bought at a 2.5% original issue discount (net $488M) plus a $5.25M commitment fee; the land banking leg carries option fees plus an $8.0M commitment fee. On the Q3 2026 call management said the preferred was underwritten on asset coverage (owned homesites and completed-home inventory) and has a risk profile like its development loans.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: 2026 guidance given on the Q4 2025 call (2026-02-26): base case of about $2.0B of invested-capital growth outside Lennar, taking total invested capital to about $10.5B with more than 40% from non-Lennar partners; about $1.0B by mid-year funded from existing debt capacity; guidance excludes M&A. Reaffirmed in the Q1 2026 release. By Q3 2026 the non-Lennar share was 36% and 42% pro forma for Dream Finders/Beazer. No explicit long-run target mix has been stated.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Forward-flow backlog: on the Q4 2025 call management said forward-flow agreements total about $9.0B across roughly 10 counterparties, and that about $3.0B of the existing portfolio cycles off each year and must be replaced. HousingWire reported the same figures and that the forward flow should cover replacement and growth even without new partners.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q4 2025 earnings call transcript (Motley Fool, 2026-02-26)

facts.fact: Non-Lennar invested capital path: about $1.1B (2025-06-30), $1.8B (2025-09-30), $2.37B (2025-12-31), $2,733M (2026-03-31), $2,850M (2026-06-30), $3,371M (2026-09-30). In Q2 2026 non-Lennar grew only $117M net because $438M of non-Lennar takedowns offset $555M of new funding; in Q3 2026 it grew $521M.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q2 2026 earnings presentation (8-K Ex. 99.2, 2026-08-04); Q3 figure from the Q3 2026 deck; 2025 figures from call transcripts and the Q1 2026 release

facts.fact: Underwriting as described by management: (1) cross-termination pooling covered about 97% of the portfolio at mid-2025, 96% at year-end 2025 and about 95% at Q1 2026; (2) no MSA above 6% of the portfolio (Q2 2025); (3) builders' price, pace and margin assumptions are tested against Millrose's own lot-pricing dataset across 30 states, then legal and development diligence; (4) an internal monthly MSA risk-rating model; (5) deposit percentages are not disclosed and the CEO declines to give contract-level terms.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool, 2026-05-06); pooling percentages also from the Q2 2025 and Q4 2025 transcripts

facts.fact: Who Millrose says it will and will not finance: management repeatedly separates builders using land banking for capital efficiency (wanted) from those using it for risk mitigation (declined). On the Q3 2025 call it said it passed on a 'substantial amount' of deals that quarter because its data did not support the builders' underwriting, and would rather pass than take more risk for a little more spread. On the Q1 2026 call it said it gives declined builders anonymized feedback comparing their lot pricing with its comps.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2025 earnings call transcript (Investing.com); feedback practice from the Q1 2026 transcript

facts.fact: View of rivals: management never names a competitor. On the Q3 2025 call Richman called Millrose the 'only national public platform' dedicated to homesite capital and said builders value certainty of capital over cost. On the Q1 2026 call management said newer land-banking entrants are finding a tougher market harder, that private land-banking alternatives cannot match Millrose's capital certainty and transparency, and that scale, data and track record widen its moat.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q1 2026 earnings call transcript (Yahoo Finance / Motley Fool, 2026-05-06)

facts.fact: Pipeline as of the Q3 2026 call: no numeric 2027 deployment target given. Nitkin said the pipeline remains active, land prices have been 'sticky', and builders including top-15 builders that are not yet clients are approaching Millrose for land positions. Takedown proceeds are to be used first to bring debt-to-capitalization back from about 36% to the 33% target, with room to lever up again for further M&A financing.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: M&A financing is now a named product line. Millrose's 2026-08-07 release called Dream Finders/Beazer the third time it has provided land banking capital for a builder acquisition (the release does not list the earlier two; the Q3 2026 deck's transaction list points to Lennar/Rausch Coleman in February 2025 and New Home/Landsea in mid-2025). Richman said he sees significant opportunity as consolidation continues; on the Q1 2026 call he described M&A support as 'a tool in the tool belt'.
facts.source_title: Millrose press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-08-07

facts.fact: Product scope widened in 2026 beyond for-sale lot options: build-to-rent (Yardly), multifamily land (JPI, July 2026), preferred equity in a builder (Dream Finders, September-October 2026) and a single-family rental pilot (1,233 completed Lennar homes in 18 states for about $333M, $120M of equity plus $213M of limited-recourse debt at SOFR+120 bps; a further build-to-rent community contract of about $150M gross had not closed at 2026-10-27). Richman called multifamily opportunistic and said Millrose would be very selective there.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27); multifamily comment from HousingWire 2026-08-07

facts.fact: The Management Agreement was amended on 2026-08-27: the investment guidelines now expressly allow single-family homes held and operated as rentals under an approved rental strategy; property-level operating costs of rental homes and the cost of holding land after a counterparty fails to exercise its option are reimbursable by Millrose; and the manager's investment allocation policy (Exhibit C) was replaced in full: opportunities directed to Millrose go 100% to Millrose when it has capacity, shared opportunities rotate between Millrose and Kennedy Lewis accounts, with quarterly reporting to the board and limits on Kennedy Lewis fundraising for land banking.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Management Agreement dated 2026-08-27 (Millrose 8-K Ex. 10.2, filed 2026-09-01)

facts.fact: The Founder's Rights Agreement with Lennar was amended on 2026-08-27: 'Excluded Capital' (capital outside Lennar's priority right) is the first $2B of debt and equity from any source plus all capital raised solely to fund rental-home ('BTR Properties') purchases; Lennar's consent is required before a Lennar-program property is pledged in a secured financing that also pledges another customer's property. Signed for Millrose by COO Robert Nitkin and for the Lennar entities by Diane Bessette and Katherine Lee Martin.
facts.source_title: Amendment to Founder's Rights Agreement dated 2026-08-27 (Millrose 8-K Ex. 10.1, filed 2026-09-01)

facts.fact: Allocation between Kennedy Lewis funds and Millrose is a live feature of every large deal: the Taylor Morrison Yardly facility ($3B, 2025-07) and the Dream Finders commitment letters ($800M land bank plus $450M preferred, 2026-08-06) were signed by Kennedy Lewis Investment Management, not Millrose, and then allocated. On the Q2 2025 call management said Kennedy Lewis fund capital is finite so most of Yardly should land in Millrose over time.
facts.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 8-K (merger agreement and commitment letters), filed 2026-08-07

facts.fact: Capital posture after Dream Finders (Q3 2026 call): debt-to-capitalization about 36% against a 33% target; a $250M buyback authorized in October 2026, to be funded from retained earnings (about 90% of earnings paid out, about 10% to buybacks while the stock is below the $35.24 book value) and not from borrowing; no equity issuance below book. The management fee was $30.3M for Q3 2026, at 1.25% of gross tangible assets; Kennedy Lewis proposed excluding the rental homes from the fee base.
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

facts.fact: Taylor Morrison, a Kennedy Lewis / Millrose counterparty, was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on 2026-07-24 for $72.50 per share in cash and has deregistered. The filing does not mention the Yardly facility or land banking. Whether a Berkshire-owned Taylor Morrison keeps using third-party land banking is not disclosed (open question raised by this agent, not a reported fact).
facts.source_title: Taylor Morrison 8-K (completion of merger with Berkshire Hathaway), filed 2026-07-24

facts.fact: A short-seller report (Hunterbrook, 2026-10-02; the firm disclosed a short position in MRP and LEN) alleged that Millrose had become a large buyer of Lennar's finished homes, with 700+ purchases in 15 states (about $200M) in roughly a month, concentrated at Lennar's quarter-end, and that Lennar's Stuart Miller (described by Hunterbrook as Lennar CEO) holds about 43% of Millrose's voting power. On the Q3 2026 call Richman said the Lennar relationship is commercial and arm's length and denied Lennar pushed Millrose into the rental pilot. Treat Hunterbrook's figures as allegations.
facts.source_title: Hunterbrook Media, 'Lennar's Big New Customer Is Its Own Spinoff, Millrose' (2026-10-02)

facts.fact: Who speaks for Millrose on earnings calls (useful for reading tone): Jesse Ross (Head of FP&A) opens; Darren Richman covers strategy and capital allocation; Robert Nitkin covers yields, underwriting and deal structure; Garett Rosenblum covers financials; Adil Pasha (CTO) and Stephen Hensley (market risk) appear occasionally. Covering analysts asking questions in 2026: Julien Blouin (Goldman Sachs), Eric Wolfe (Citi), Craig Kucera (Lucid, then B. Riley), Ryan Gilbert (BTIG).
facts.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings call transcript (Webull copy of Motley Fool transcript, 2026-10-27)

builder_relationships.builder_name: Dream Finders Homes (acquirer of Beazer Homes)
builder_relationships.description: Millrose supplied about $1.1B ($1,068M itemized) to fund Dream Finders' acquisition of Beazer Homes, closed 2026-10-20: (1) about $580M of land banking (net of option deposits) on about 7,000 homesites, weighted average life about 2.5 years, more than half finished lots, with option fees plus an $8.0M commitment fee; (2) about $488M (net of OID) of preferred equity paying a 12% dividend on a $500M balance plus a $5.25M commitment fee, funded $171M on 2026-09-14 and $317M at closing. Announced by Millrose (originally as an up-to-$1.25B commitment).

builder_relationships.builder_name: New Home Co (now Risewell Homes) / Landsea Homes
builder_relationships.description: Millrose's Q3 2026 deck lists the Landsea take-private by New Home (transaction date 2025-05-12) as a platform transaction in which Millrose acquired 4,186 homesites and about $700M of land assets.
When Lennar bought Rausch Coleman's operating business (transaction date 2025-02-10), Millrose acquired about 25,000 homesites and about $900M of land assets, optioned to Lennar.

Builder-side view of the Beazer financing. Commitment letters dated 2026-08-06 were with Kennedy Lewis Investment Management (not Millrose): an $800M land bank facility and a $450M convertible preferred investment, alongside a $900M bank bridge (BofA / Goldman). At closing on 2026-10-20 Dream Finders received $572.1M of land-bank proceeds from Millrose and/or affiliates, used to redeem Beazer's $350M 7.25% notes due 2029 and repay Beazer's credit facility. Beazer was bought for $33.50 per share, about $878.4M.

builder_relationships.builder_name: Dream Finders Homes (Series B Convertible Preferred)
builder_relationships.description: Terms of the preferred Millrose bought: 12.00% cumulative dividend, deferrable, stepping up 0.50% after year 6 and every six months after to a 15% cap; perpetual; callable by the company after year 3 at 102%, year 4 at 101%, then par; holder conversion only after year 6 at a 20% discount to the 90-day average price (25% discount on covenant breach); 2.5% original issue discount; board observer right and a right of first refusal on new preferred. Dream Finders sold $675M in total ($225M on 2026-09-14, $450M on 2026-10-20) to unnamed institutional purchasers. Millrose says it holds a $500M balance ($171M and $317M funded net of discount), so about $175M went to other purchasers (calculated: 675 minus 500; not identified).
builder_relationships.source_title: Dream Finders Homes 8-K (Series B preferred first closing), filed 2026-09-15

builder_relationships.description: Sequence of Millrose's announcements: 2026-05-11, intent to provide land banking for Dream Finders' proposed Beazer acquisition, backed by a Goldman Sachs 'highly confident' letter for up to $500M of financing, with Millrose to buy the homesites Beazer owns and a warning that leverage would temporarily exceed target; 2026-08-07, the manager committed up to $1.25B of acquisition financing once the merger agreement was signed. Final funded amount was about $1.07B.

builder_relationships.builder_name: Beazer Homes USA (acquired by Dream Finders Homes 2026-10-20)
builder_relationships.description: Beazer was already a land-banking client before the merger: in Millrose's 2026-08-07 release CEO Richman called both Dream Finders and Beazer valued clients and said his team had partnered with Beazer across multiple market cycles. Size of the pre-merger Beazer and Dream Finders positions is not disclosed. Post-merger, Millrose land-banks about 7,000 former Beazer/Dream Finders homesites for about $580M.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-08-07

builder_relationships.builder_name: New Home Co (now Risewell Homes) / Landsea Homes
builder_relationships.description: New Home's 2025-05-12 announcement of its $11.30-per-share, roughly $1.2B enterprise value take-private of Landsea said Millrose was providing committed land banking capital alongside $650M of new Apollo equity; no Millrose dollar figure was given there. On Millrose's Q2 2025 call management said it closed an approximately $500M homesite portfolio (net cash funding) with cross-termination provisions like its other contracts. Millrose's own deck states 4,186 homesites and $700M of land assets; the gap between about $500M net funding and $700M is not explained publicly (likely deposits and future development funding; inferred). The deal closed 2025-06-25 per HousingWire.
builder_relationships.source_title: New Home Co / Landsea Homes joint press release (Landsea 8-K Ex. 99.1), 2025-05-12; funding figure from the Q2 2025 call transcript (Reported)

builder_relationships.description: $3B land and construction financing facility for Yardly, Taylor Morrison's build-to-rent brand, announced 2025-07-23 with Kennedy Lewis Investment Management as provider; covers existing and new land, development and construction. On Millrose's Q2 2025 call management said the commitment runs over a 2.5-year exclusivity term, is split between a Kennedy Lewis fund and Millrose under the allocation policy, with most expected to be allocated to Millrose; structure matches for-sale option deals but with a single takeout at the end; first Millrose closings in Q3 2025, and Yardly was a 'decent portion' of Q3 2025 non-Lennar volume. Millrose's share in dollars is not disclosed.

Taylor Morrison's 2025-07-23 release says it already had a land banking agreement with Kennedy Lewis supporting its for-sale operations, making Yardly the second financing vehicle between them. Whether those for-sale lots sit in Millrose or in Kennedy Lewis funds is not stated; Millrose's CEO named Taylor Morrison as a Millrose client on the Q2 2025 call. Taylor Morrison was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway on 2026-07-24.

builder_relationships.builder_name: JPI (multifamily developer; subsidiary of Sumitomo Forestry)
builder_relationships.description: Announced 2026-07-30: Millrose closed the first acquisition under a new land banking facility set up by JPI and Kennedy Lewis Investment Management for Class A multifamily sites in JPI's target markets. Millrose buys the sites and funds development; JPI pays option fees and takes sites down as projects mature. Millrose's first multifamily counterparty. Facility size, first-site location and dollars are not disclosed. JPI's CFO/CIO Mollie Fadule called it an off-balance-sheet capital solution. Per HousingWire, management said it mirrors the Yardly structure.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose / JPI press release via Business Wire (Finviz copy), 2026-07-30

builder_relationships.description: Millrose bought 1,233 completed homes from Lennar across 18 states for an aggregate cost of about $333M (about $270K to $280K per home), financed with $213M of limited-recourse secured debt at SOFR+120 bps and about $120M of equity. Underwritten at roughly a 5% going-in cap rate, about 8% unlevered and 10-12% levered IRR; about 10% of homes rented as of 2026-10-26; leasing managed by Evergreen Residential. Management says no further purchases since quarter-end and that rent-to-own is still being designed.
builder_relationships.source_title: Millrose Q3 2026 earnings press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-10-27); underwriting detail from the Q3 2026 call transcript (Reported)
